title: ELISA Protocol
author: ELISAassays
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.f6ebrbe
materials: After experiment, store all reagents according to the specified storage temperature respectively until their expiry.
Cover the plate with sealer we provided.
Gently tap the plate to ensure thorough mixing.

steps.title: Initial incubation (120 min, 37 °C)
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 120 minutes at 37 °C.

steps.title: Invert plate and pat dry
steps.instruction: Invert the plate and pat it against thick clean absorbent paper.

steps.title: Secondary incubation (60 min, 37 °C)
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 60 minutes at 37 °C.

steps.title: First wash (1/5) with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 1 of 5 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well) and ensure complete removal of liquid.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well.
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Add Stop Solution and mix
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Stop Solution to each well; if color change is not uniform, gently tap the plate to ensure thorough mixing.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL Stop Solution to each well.
If color is uneven, gently tap the plate to mix.

steps.title: Measure optical density at 450 nm
steps.instruction: Determine the optical density of each well at 450 nm using a pre‑heated microplate reader with appropriate parameters set.

steps.title: Add standards, blanks, or samples
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of Standard, Blank, or Sample to each well, using Sample diluent for blank wells; avoid touching the well walls and minimize foaming.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL Standard, Blank, or Sample to each well (blank receives Sample diluent).
Avoid contacting the well walls and minimize foaming.

steps.title: Gentle mixing of wells
steps.instruction: Mix the contents of each well gently.

steps.title: Remove liquid without washing
steps.instruction: Aspirate and discard the liquid from each well; do not perform a wash step.

steps.title: Add Detection Reagent A (100 µL)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of Detection Reagent A working solution to each well.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL Detection Reagent A working solution to each well.

steps.title: Incubate with Reagent A (1 h, 37 °C)
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 1 hour at 37 °C; if Detection Reagent A appears cloudy, warm to room temperature until the solution becomes uniform.

steps.title: Wash 1 of 3 with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 1 of 3 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well); complete removal of liquid is essential.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well (using a squirt bottle, multi‑channel pipette, manifold dispenser, or automated washer).
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Remove residual Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: After the last wash, completely remove any remaining Wash Buffer by aspirating or decanting.

steps.title: Add Detection Reagent B (100 µL)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of Detection Reagent B working solution to each well.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL Detection Reagent B working solution to each well.

steps.title: Add Substrate Solution (90 µL)
steps.instruction: Add 90 µL of Substrate Solution to each well.

substeps.instruction: Add 90 µL Substrate Solution to each well.

steps.title: Seal plate and incubate (15‑30 min, 37 °C)
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with a new plate sealer and incubate for 15–30 minutes at 37 °C while protecting from light; do not exceed 30 minutes and terminate the reaction if a gradient appears in standard wells.

substeps.instruction: Cover with a new plate sealer.
Incubate 15–30 min at 37 °C, protect from light.
Do not exceed 30 min; stop the reaction if a gradient appears in standard wells.

steps.title: Wash 2 of 3 with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 2 of 3 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well); ensure complete removal of liquid.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well.
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Wash 3 of 3 with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 3 of 3 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well); ensure complete removal of liquid.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well.
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Wash 2 of 5 with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 2 of 5 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well); ensure complete removal of liquid.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well.
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Wash 3 of 5 with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 3 of 5 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well); ensure complete removal of liquid.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well.
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Wash 4 of 5 with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 4 of 5 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well); ensure complete removal of liquid.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well.
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Wash 5 of 5 with Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Perform wash 5 of 5 using Wash Buffer (~400 µL per well); ensure complete removal of liquid.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all liquid from each well.
Add approximately 400 µL Wash Buffer to each well.
Aspirate completely to remove Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Final removal of Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: After the last wash, completely remove any remaining Wash Buffer by aspirating or decanting.

steps.title: Invert plate and pat dry
steps.instruction: Invert the plate and pat it against thick clean absorbent paper.
